Hi all — here's the technical snapshot for the bundle. I'm including caveats inline so auditors have context.

Summary RTO/RPO (canonical):
- Control plane (orchestration + auth): RTO 2 hours (cold restart with config restore), RPO near-zero for config (backups every 5 minutes), owner: infra-team.
- Serving layer (hosted inference API): RTO 30 minutes to switch traffic to warm standby cluster (automated), RPO approximately 1 minute for KV/prefix cache under standard workloads; critical request routing state is persisted to durable storage with RPO near-zero.
- Model registry (object store + manifest): RTO 1 hour for restore from cross-region snapshot, RPO near-zero (objects replicated asynchronously across regions; last-replicated timestamp included in snapshot).
- Logging & telemetry: RTO N/A (logs are immutable in S3), RPO N/A (we retain continuous streams).

Cross-region failover records: Attached are two traces from 2026-11-02 and 2026-12-14 showing failover initiation and time to full traffic restoration. I've redacted internal node IDs per policy but preserved timestamps and durations.

Tabletop exercise: see attached bcp-tabletop-summary-20241012.pdf (AAR).

Caveats / clarifications for auditors:
- The "KV cache RPO ~1 minute" refers to prefix-level in-memory cache that we warm via snapshotting; in the worst-case warm-start scenario some in-flight KV states may be up to 5 minutes behind depending on write volume. We call this out in the gap-log.
- Model load times depend on model size; for models >20B tokens we typically observe cold-start load of 8-12 minutes to reach steady memory residency. Our serving SLA accounts for warm pool sizing to avoid cold-starts for pinned models.

Attachments in this message: bcp-tabletop-summary-20241012.pdf, cross-region-failover-trace-20261102.log, cross-region-failover-trace-20261214.log

I'll hand the artifacts to Aditya for consolidation. If auditors need raw traces, we can provide them under an NDA.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
